## Why
In `src/fine_art_archive/eink/playlist.py:400-401`, `sort_value()` implements artist sorting as `return (row["artist"].lower(), row["year"] or 9999)`. Because `0` is falsy in Python, artworks dated to astronomical year `0` (1 BC) are coerced to `9999` and sorted after modern works instead of before year 1.

## Scope
- `src/fine_art_archive/eink/playlist.py`
- `tests/test_eink_pipeline.py`

## Non-Goals
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: converting years to string representations or special casing 0 without distinguishing `None` from integer `0` is a failure of this issue.
- Do not modify playlist filtering or random shuffle logic.

## Tasks
- [ ] Update `sort_value()` in `src/fine_art_archive/eink/playlist.py` to use `row["year"] if row["year"] is not None else 9999` for artist sort.
- [ ] Add unit tests in `tests/test_eink_pipeline.py` asserting works dated year `0` sort before positive years when sorting playlists by artist.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `pytest tests/test_eink_pipeline.py` passes with 100% success.
- Sorting playlist rows containing works dated year `0` and year `1500` by artist places the year `0` work before the year `1500` work.
- Deliberate break: revert `row["year"] if row["year"] is not None else 9999` to `row["year"] or 9999` in `src/fine_art_archive/eink/playlist.py`, run `pytest tests/test_eink_pipeline.py`, and verify that the year 0 sort test fails; revert to pass.

## Implementation Notes
- Use explicit `None` checking (`row["year"] if row["year"] is not None else 9999`) in `src/fine_art_archive/eink/playlist.py`.
issues.title: fix(playlist): prevent year 0 falsiness in playlist artist sort

- `tests/test_variants.py`

## Why
In `src/fine_art_archive/preference/rocchio.py:124-173`, `build()` collects scored works with `[(features_of(sc), s) for sc, s in rated if s is not None]`. When a score `s` is `float('nan')` or non-numeric, `s > split` and `s < split` comparisons evaluate to False, treating all ratings as ties at median `NaN`. This produces an empty `PreferenceVector` with `split_value=nan` despite valid scores being present in the input.

## Scope
- `src/fine_art_archive/preference/rocchio.py`
- `tests/test_rocchio_preference.py`

## Non-Goals
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: catching `TypeError` during centroid math without filtering non-finite scores during initial rated filtering is a failure of this issue.
- Do not alter Rocchio `BETA` or `GAMMA` centroid weighting constants.

## Tasks
- [ ] Filter non-finite and boolean ratings in `build()` within `src/fine_art_archive/preference/rocchio.py` using `isinstance(s, (int, float)) and not isinstance(s, bool) and math.isfinite(s)`.
- [ ] Add unit tests in `tests/test_rocchio_preference.py` asserting `build()` ignores NaN ratings and correctly builds preference vectors from remaining valid scores.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `pytest tests/test_rocchio_preference.py` passes with 100% success.
- Supplying `[(work_a, float("nan")), (work_b, 9.0), (work_c, 3.0)]` to `build()` calculates a valid median split and non-empty preference weights without NaN corruption.

## Why
In `src/fine_art_archive/selection/lenses.py:236-274`, `apply_saturation_cap()` computes allowed candidate counts per bucket using `int(round(batch_cap * float(share) * tolerance))`. If an archive share is `float('nan')` or `float('inf')`, or if `tolerance` is non-finite, Python raises `ValueError: cannot convert float NaN to integer` or `OverflowError`. Furthermore, when `batch_cap <= 0`, `allowed[bucket] = max(1, ...)` forces each bucket to allow at least 1 candidate, causing non-empty selections when zero items were requested.

## Scope
- `src/fine_art_archive/selection/lenses.py`
- `tests/test_selection_lenses.py`

## Non-Goals
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: catching `ValueError` at call sites or returning unvalidated pools without sanitizing `batch_cap`, shares, and tolerance is a failure of this issue.
- Do not modify candidate ranking order or round-robin selection logic outside saturation capping.

## Tasks
- [ ] Add entry guard for `batch_cap <= 0` returning `([], SaturationReport(...))` and validate `0.0 <= float(share) <= 1.0` and `float(tolerance) >= 0.0` with `math.isfinite` in `src/fine_art_archive/selection/lenses.py`.
- [ ] Add unit tests in `tests/test_selection_lenses.py` asserting `apply_saturation_cap` handles `batch_cap <= 0`, NaN/inf shares, and non-finite tolerances without raising exceptions.

> **Not dispatchable to an agent — needs physical hardware that does not exist yet.** Tracking only; do not add `agents:auto-pilot`.

## Why

Epic #23 is closed because its blocker (which panel, push vs SD) is resolved and **both** transports are built, tested and merged. But #23's goal says deliver to the *physical* panels, and no panel has been bought. Everything is verified against the app, nothing against glass.

Two specific things are unknown until a real device exists, and both are recorded here so they are not rediscovered:

**1. The palette is estimated, not measured.** `src/fine_art_archive/eink/palette.py` ships Spectra 6 primaries that are reasonable guesses. Every palette carries `measured: False`, and every exported SD card states so in `playlist.json` and `README.txt`. No vendor at these sizes publishes a colour profile, gamut volume or Delta-E — `docs/EINK_DEVICE_SURVEY.md` calls this the survey's central open gap. Replacing six RGB triples upgrades every card and feed retroactively.

**2. Colour may not be good enough at all.** The one independent hands-on report of a 28.5" colour unit describes photographs as "dark, desaturated, and low resolution", with no pure white — only "a yellowish grey" — and **monochrome reproductions faring markedly better than colour**. The survey's own recommendation is to measure a unit before committing the pipeline to colour e-paper. If mono wins, the `gray16` target already exists.

## Scope

First-light verification of the existing pipeline against one purchased panel. No new features.

## Non-Goals

- No new render targets, transports or UI. Both transports are done.
- Not buying the hardware — that is the owner's decision, and the survey's US-availability read is in `docs/EINK_DEVICE_SURVEY.md`.
- Not a colour-management system. Six measured primaries is the deliverable, not an ICC workflow.

## Tasks

- [ ] Photograph a rendered card under controlled light and sample the six Spectra 6 primaries from a full-coverage test pattern; record the measured RGB.
- [ ] Replace the estimated tuples in `palette.py` `SPECTRA6` with the measured values and set `measured=True`.
- [ ] Re-run `dither_error` on a reference work with measured vs estimated palettes and record the change in `perceived_rgb_distance`.
- [ ] Exercise the chosen transport end to end on the device: for SD, write a card with `scripts/make_eink_card.py --write` and confirm the panel plays it in filename order; for network, point the device at `/feed/{id}/current` and confirm it advances across a rotation interval.
- [ ] Compare a colour render against a `gray16` render of the same work on the panel and record which reads better, per the survey's warning.
- [ ] Update `docs/EINK_DEVICE_SURVEY.md` to replace "no vendor publishes a colour profile" with the measured result for the device bought.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `python3 -m pytest tests/test_eink_pipeline.py` still passes with the measured palette in place (the palette-invariant tests must hold for real values, not just estimates).
- [ ] `get_palette("spectra6").measured is True`, and a freshly exported card's `playlist.json` shows `"palette_measured": true` with no `palette_warning`.
- [ ] A photograph of the panel showing an exported work is attached to this issue — the observable gate, since no automated check can see glass.
- [ ] The panel is confirmed to advance through at least two works via the chosen transport, evidenced by two photographs or a device log.
- [ ] A one-line verdict is recorded in the survey: colour usable / mono preferred, with the measured perceived-error figures behind it.

**Parked 2026-08-08 — hardware purchase deferred, no work in flight.**

The 13.3"/31.5" colour e-paper category was reviewed and judged not yet mature enough to buy into. Options examined: Inkplate 13SPECTRA (pre-order from a startup that may never ship); Seeed XIAO kit $163.90 and Waveshare 13.3" ~$260 (bare panels, real assembly); E Ink's own shopkit $449 (**explicitly refuses consumer orders**); and the finished frames — paperlesspaper openpaper L €339, BLOOMIN8 13.3", Reflection Frame $349.99, Aluratek $349.99, Aura Ink $499 — all early-generation with thin reviews.

**This does not block the colour work.** The corpus **gamut-fit score** answers "is Spectra 6 good enough for *this* archive" with **no hardware at all**, and yields a permanent playlist sort key and acquisition signal. It should have run first regardless, and is now the top e-ink item.

**When hardware is eventually bought, amend the task list here BEFORE the session** — without the first item the measurement has to be repeated:

- [ ] Put a **ColorChecker in the same frame**, shoot raw with **fixed white balance** — auto-WB destroys the exact quantity being measured
- [ ] Record the **illuminant** and ideally its CCT — e-paper is reflective, so its colour is ink reflectance × room light
- [ ] Record the **panel generation** — Spectra 6 and Spectra 6 Plus have different primaries
- [ ] Print dithered **mid-tone ramps and a large flat field**, not only full-coverage patches

**The feature to buy on when the category matures is pre-dithered ingest, not size or price.** Across all 179 devices surveyed, exactly one — BLOOMIN8 — exposes `POST /image/dataUpload` for pre-dithered raw data. Every other frame re-dithers in vendor firmware, which would silently discard this project's entire render pipeline: you could measure the palette but never actually drive it.

Next scheduled re-survey: the quarterly landscape review, **2026-11-01**.
